summary: The section library, layout presets, regional conventions and formatting standards behind `/armor`. Everything here is authored in `resume-library.json` and rendered from it — edit the JSON, then run `node tools/resume_library.mjs build`.

legend.V: VERIFIED against the cited source page, read in full during an authoring session. Carries the source id and the date it was read.
legend.S: SECONDARY / UNVERIFIED. Attributed to a cited source by search-engine summaries or third-party write-ups, but the source page itself was NOT read. Treat as a lead to confirm, not as a quotation.
legend.G: GENERAL PRACTICE. A widely-established convention across career-services guidance and applicant-tracking documentation. Not attributed to any single source and does not need to be.

provenance.rule: No rule in this file may be presented to a player as coming from a named institution unless its tag is V. This is the same provenance discipline the System Log applies to claimed rulings: an uncited claim is struck or downgraded, never repeated with confidence it has not earned.
provenance.authoringNote: At v1.0.0 NO rule is tagged V, and that is a deliberate record of what the authoring session could actually establish. The session (2026-08-27) could not read any external page: the environment's egress proxy refused every outbound fetch, for every domain — curl returned CONNECT 403, and the fetch tool returned EGRESS_BLOCKED for the source URL and for a control URL alike, so the block was environmental rather than specific to the source host. Every S tag below is therefore a lead awaiting confirmation, not a quotation. `node tools/resume_library.mjs sources` is the mechanism that confirms them from a networked environment: it records a content snapshot per source, after which a rule can be promoted from S to V by a human or agent who has actually read the page.

sources.label: Harvard FAS Mignone Center for Career Success — Create a Strong Resume
sources.note: Requested by Will as the research basis. Never successfully retrieved — see provenance.authoringNote. The first run of `resume_source_check.mjs` from a networked environment records lastRead, contentSha256 and a text snapshot, after which drift is detectable.

sources.label: Harvard College Bullet Point Resume Template
sources.note: Surfaced by search alongside the primary. Likely carries the concrete section order and bullet formula.

sources.label: Harvard College Resumes & Cover Letters Guide
sources.note: The long-form guide the shorter pages summarise.

formatting.t: One page for most candidates. A second page is earned by content, not filled to look substantial — and in most markets is normal past roughly ten years of relevant experience.
Single column. Multi-column layouts read out of order in most applicant-tracking parsers, which silently scrambles dates against employers.
No graphics, photos, colour blocks, icons, text boxes or headshots on an ATS-bound resume. They either drop out or corrupt the parse.
Standard serif or sans-serif face at 10–12pt body size. Consistency matters more than which face.
Margins around 1 inch / 2.5cm; never below 0.5 inch / 1.25cm, which reads as cramped and breaks print.
Dates right-aligned and formatted identically everywhere. Mixed formats are the single most common self-inflicted parse failure.
The resume and its cover letter use the same font family and size — they are one document set.
Submit as PDF unless the posting asks for .docx. PDF preserves layout; .docx is what some ATS explicitly demand.
Name the file predictably: Firstname-Lastname-Role.pdf. Never 'resume-final-v3.pdf'.
Section headings in the conventional words for the target market. A parser looks for 'Experience' and 'Education'; it does not know what 'My Journey' means.

bullets.t: Every bullet opens with a past-tense action verb. No 'Responsible for', no 'Duties included', no leading pronoun.
Quantify the result wherever a real number exists — scale, money, time, percentage, headcount, volume.
Formula: ACTION VERB + WHAT YOU DID + HOW / WITH WHAT + MEASURED RESULT. Not every bullet reaches all four, but a bullet with none of the last two is a job description, not evidence.
Accomplishment, not duty. What changed because you were there, rather than what you were assigned.
Three to six bullets for a recent, relevant role; one to three for older or less relevant ones. Depth follows relevance, not chronology.
One to two lines per bullet. A bullet that wraps to three is two bullets or an over-written one.
Mirror the posting's own vocabulary where it is honestly true of you — the same skill named two ways scores as neither.
Never fabricate a metric. An honest unquantified bullet beats an invented number, and an invented number is the one thing a reference check reliably catches.

ats.t: No tables. A parser flattens them and the columns interleave.
No headers or footers for content that matters — many parsers discard that region entirely, including contact details placed there.
No text inside images. It is invisible to every parser.
Spell out an acronym once with the acronym alongside: 'Security Information and Event Management (SIEM)'. Postings search for either.
Standard bullet characters only. Wingdings and custom glyphs arrive as question marks.

actionVerbs.note: Grouped by what the verb claims. Pick for accuracy, not for force — an inflated verb is a claim the interview will test.

sections.label: Header / Contact
sections.purpose: Says who you are and how to reach you. Always first — this is the one section that cannot move.

rules.t: Name, phone with country code, professional email, city + country, LinkedIn. Nothing else is mandatory.
Never in the page header/footer region — parsers discard it.
Full street address is obsolete in most markets; city and country are enough and are what recruiters filter on.
One professional email. Not a work address — screening a candidate on their current employer's mail is a hazard for both sides.

sections.label: Professional Summary
sections.purpose: Two to four lines positioning you for THIS role. The highest-leverage lines on the page because they are the ones actually read.

rules.t: Rewritten per application. A generic summary is worse than none — it costs prime space to say nothing.
Name the discipline, the seniority, and the two or three things this posting is actually buying.
No first person, no adjective piles. 'Passionate self-starter' is unfalsifiable and reads as filler.
Distinct from an Objective: a summary says what you bring, an objective says what you want. Prefer the summary except in a deliberate career change.

sections.label: Objective
sections.purpose: States the role sought. Largely retired in favour of a summary; still useful for a career change or an early-career candidate where the direction is not obvious from the history.

rules.t: Use instead of a summary, never alongside it.
If it could be pasted onto any application unchanged, cut it.

sections.label: Core Skills
sections.purpose: A scannable keyword surface. Does double duty: a human reads it in three seconds, a parser matches it against the posting.

rules.t: Group into labelled clusters rather than one long comma run — 'Cloud & Infrastructure:', 'Governance & Risk:'.
Only skills you would defend in an interview. This section is the most over-claimed on the page and the easiest to test.
Drop proficiency bars and star ratings. They are unparseable and self-assessed, so they carry no information.
Place high when the role is skills-gated (technical, contract, career change); place lower when the employer names carry the story.

sections.label: Professional Experience
sections.purpose: The evidence base. Reverse-chronological by default.

rules.t: Per role: title, employer, location, dates. Consistent order and format across every entry.
Reverse-chronological — most recent first — unless deliberately using a functional or hybrid layout.
Bullets selected for THIS posting from the full history, not the same block reused everywhere.
A promotion within one employer is nested under that employer, not duplicated as a separate company.
Employment gaps: state them plainly and briefly if they exceed several months. An unexplained gap draws more attention than an explained one.
Add a one-line company descriptor when the employer is not internationally recognised — 'Origin (ASX-listed energy retailer, 4,000 staff)'. Essential when applying across borders.

sections.label: Education
sections.purpose: Formal qualifications.

rules.t: Degree, institution, location, completion year. Reverse-chronological.
Above Experience while a student or within roughly two years of graduating; below it thereafter.
Include grade only where the market expects it and it helps — see the region profile; GPA is a US convention and reads as odd elsewhere.
Add an equivalence note for a foreign qualification: 'Bachelor of Engineering (4 years, equivalent to AQF Level 7)'. A reader who cannot place your degree discounts it.
Secondary schooling drops off once you hold a degree.

sections.label: Projects
sections.purpose: Demonstrated capability where employment history does not yet show it — career changers, early career, or skills used outside a paid role.

rules.t: Same bullet discipline as Experience: action, substance, outcome.
Link to something inspectable where one exists.
State your own contribution on anything collaborative.

sections.label: Certifications & Licences
sections.purpose: Named credentials, especially where a role gates on them.

rules.t: Full name, issuing body, year. Include expiry where the credential has one.
Move high — even directly under the summary — when the posting lists a certification as a requirement.
Mark in-progress credentials honestly with an expected date. Never list an unearned one as held.

sections.label: Leadership & Activities
sections.purpose: Responsibility carried outside a job title. Weighted heavily for students and early career; thins out as employment history grows.

rules.t: Treat like Experience — role, organisation, dates, outcome bullets.
Retain later in a career only where it carries genuine scope: a board seat, a chaired committee, a conference track.

sections.label: Publications
sections.purpose: Published work. Expected in academic and research contexts, selective elsewhere.

rules.t: One consistent citation style throughout.
On an industry resume, select three to five and title the section 'Selected Publications'. A full list belongs on an academic CV.

sections.label: Talks & Presentations
sections.purpose: Conference talks, invited lectures, panels — external credibility a job title does not convey.

rules.t: Title, venue, year. Note invited or keynote status where it applies.

sections.label: Awards & Honours
sections.purpose: Third-party recognition — the only section where someone else is doing the claiming.

rules.t: Award, awarding body, year, and one clause on selectivity where it is not obvious: 'top 2% of 1,400 staff'.
May be folded into Education or Experience when there are only one or two.

sections.label: Volunteering
sections.purpose: Unpaid contribution. Also a legitimate way to account for a career break.

rules.t: Include where it shows relevant skill, sustained commitment, or covers a gap. Otherwise optional.
Political and religious affiliations are a discrimination risk in most markets — include only where genuinely relevant to the role.

sections.label: Languages
sections.purpose: Working languages and level. Materially more important outside monolingual markets.

rules.t: Name a recognised scale: CEFR (A1–C2) in Europe, or plain words — Native / Fluent / Professional working / Conversational.
Do not list the posting's own language as a skill when you are applying in it natively.

sections.label: Work Authorisation
sections.purpose: Whether you can legally work in the target country. The single most consequential line on an international application and the one most often left off.

rules.t: State it plainly in one line when applying across a border. Recruiters screen on it first, and silence is read as 'needs sponsorship'.
State the entitlement, not the personal circumstance: 'Australian citizen — unrestricted work rights' or 'UK Skilled Worker visa, valid to 2029'.
Where sponsorship IS required, saying so early saves both sides a cycle. It is not a weakness to hide; it is a filter to pass honestly.
Sits in the header line or immediately under the summary — it is a screening fact, not an afterthought.

sections.label: Security Clearance
sections.purpose: Held clearance level and status. Gates entire job families in defence, government and adjacent industry.

rules.t: Level, sponsoring country, and current status only. Never project details, agency names, or anything the clearance itself covers.
Place high where the posting requires it — it is often a hard filter before anything else is read.
Clearances are country-specific and rarely transfer. State the issuing country.

sections.label: Professional Memberships
sections.purpose: Professional body membership and chartered status — load-bearing in engineering, accounting, law and medicine.

rules.t: Body, membership grade, and year admitted. Chartered or registered status is a qualification, not a hobby — say it clearly.

sections.label: Interests
sections.purpose: A short human line. Genuinely conventional in some markets, space-wasting in others.

rules.t: One line, three or four specifics. 'Reading, travel, music' says nothing about anyone.
First thing to cut when the page is tight.

sections.label: Referees
sections.purpose: Named referees with contact details. Expected up front in some markets, actively discouraged in others.

rules.t: 'References available on request' is filler in every market. Either list them because the market expects it, or omit the section entirely.
Never list a referee you have not asked. It costs you the reference and the referee's goodwill at once.
Where listed: name, title, organisation, relationship to you, and a contact channel they have agreed to.

sections.label: Personal Details
sections.purpose: Photo, date of birth, nationality, marital status. Conventional in parts of Europe, Asia, the Middle East and Latin America; a legal and discrimination hazard in the US, UK, Canada and Australia.

rules.t: Governed entirely by the region profile. Include ONLY where the target market expects it.

In the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Ireland, a photo or date of birth can force an employer to discard the application to protect themselves against a discrimination claim. This is not a style preference.
Never volunteer marital status, dependants, religion, or health information in any market unless a legal requirement is documented.

sections.label: Data Processing Consent
sections.purpose: A short consent line permitting the employer to process your personal data. Conventional and sometimes required in parts of the EU, most strictly in Poland.

rules.t: One line at the foot of the document. Where required, an application without it may be discarded unread.
Meaningless outside the jurisdictions that ask for it — omit rather than include 'just in case'.

sections.label: Additional Information
sections.purpose: A deliberate catch-all for one-line facts that earn a mention but not a section: a driving licence where the job needs one, willingness to relocate, notice period.

rules.t: Keep it to a few lines. A long 'Additional' section means something in it deserved its own heading.

layouts.label: ATS Reverse-Chronological
layouts.whenToUse: The default, and correct for the large majority of applications — any online portal, any recruiter, any established career in one field.

layouts.label: Early Career / Graduate
layouts.whenToUse: Student, new graduate, or within roughly two years of finishing study. Education carries the weight that employment cannot yet.

layouts.label: Career Change / Hybrid
layouts.whenToUse: Moving between fields, where transferable capability matters more than the sequence of employers.

layouts.label: Technical / Engineering
layouts.whenToUse: Roles gated on a named stack, where the first screen is a keyword match against tools.

layouts.label: Cleared / Government
layouts.whenToUse: Defence, government or regulated roles where clearance and citizenship are hard filters applied before the resume is read properly.

layouts.label: Academic CV
layouts.whenToUse: Faculty, postdoctoral, research and fellowship applications. Length is driven by the record — multi-page is expected, not a fault.

layouts.label: International / Relocating
layouts.whenToUse: Applying across a border. Front-loads the two facts a foreign recruiter screens on before anything else — can you work here, and can I place your background.

regions.label: Australia & New Zealand
regions.length: 2–3 pages is normal and expected. The one-page rule is a US convention and reading it as universal actively hurts you here.

notes.referees: Commonly listed, or 'available on request' is tolerated here more than elsewhere. Two referees is standard.
notes.education: No GPA convention. WAM or a class of honours may be given where strong.
notes.work-authorization: Citizenship or visa status is routinely stated and often explicitly asked for. Say it.
notes.security-clearance: AGSVA levels (Baseline, NV1, NV2, PV) are widely recognised and worth naming precisely.

warnings: No photo, date of birth, marital status or nationality beyond work rights.

regions.label: United States
regions.docName: Resume ('CV' means the academic document only)
regions.length: One page is the strong default; two pages past roughly ten years of experience.

notes.education: GPA conventionally included if 3.0+ and within a few years of graduating; dropped thereafter.
notes.referees: Never on the resume. Supplied separately when asked.
notes.work-authorization: State it if you are not a citizen or permanent resident — 'Authorized to work in the US without sponsorship' is the standard line.

warnings: A photo, date of birth or marital status can force an employer to discard the application to avoid a discrimination claim. This is the strictest market on this point.

regions.label: United Kingdom & Ireland
regions.length: Two pages is the firm convention. One page reads as thin, three as undisciplined.

notes.referees: 'References available on request' is still common but adds nothing. Omitting the section is safe.
notes.education: Degree classification (First, 2:1) is expected and is the grade signal — not GPA.
notes.memberships: Chartered status (CEng, CITP, ACA) is significant and belongs high.
notes.work-authorization: Post-Brexit this matters for EU nationals too. State settled status or visa type.

warnings: No photo, date of birth, nationality or marital status.

regions.label: Canada

notes.languages: English/French bilingualism is a genuine differentiator, especially federally and in Quebec.
notes.work-authorization: State PR or citizenship status plainly.
notes.education: Foreign credentials benefit from an equivalency note (WES or similar) where you have one.

warnings: Human rights legislation makes photo, age, marital status and nationality inappropriate.

regions.label: Germany, Austria & Switzerland
regions.docName: Lebenslauf (CV), usually inside a full Bewerbung application set
regions.length: One to two pages, tabular and factual.
regions.spelling: German where applying in German; otherwise standard English.

notes.personal-details: A professional headshot remains conventional, though declining. Date and place of birth and nationality are commonly included. This is the inverse of the Anglophone markets — follow the local norm, not the US one.
notes.experience: Gaps are scrutinised more than in most markets; account for them explicitly.
notes.certifications: Reference letters (Arbeitszeugnisse) from prior employers are a distinct expected artefact — not part of the CV, but assemble them.
notes.languages: CEFR levels expected. German level is often the deciding factor.

warnings: Signing and dating the document is still conventional in traditional sectors.

regions.label: France
regions.length: One page strongly preferred, even at senior level.

notes.personal-details: Photo is common but no longer expected; age is sometimes included. Optional either way — omitting it is safe.
notes.education: The grande école / university distinction carries real weight; name the institution precisely.

warnings: Anti-discrimination guidance has moved against photos; treat them as optional, never mandatory.

regions.label: Netherlands, Belgium & the Nordics
regions.spelling: British English where applying in English.

notes.personal-details: Photo is optional and increasingly skipped. Date of birth is still fairly common in the Netherlands.
notes.summary: A short personal profile is conventional and read.
notes.languages: Expected. English fluency is assumed rather than impressive; the local language is the differentiator.

warnings: Flat organisational cultures — over-claimed seniority reads badly.

regions.label: Spain, Italy & Portugal

notes.personal-details: Photo and date of birth remain common.
notes.gdpr-clause: A data-processing consent line is conventional.

warnings: The Europass format is recognised but generic — a tailored CV usually reads better unless a public-sector posting asks for Europass specifically.

regions.label: Poland & Central/Eastern Europe
regions.spelling: Local language or English depending on the employer.

notes.gdpr-clause: In Poland this is the strictest case anywhere: a CV without a data-processing consent clause is routinely discarded unread, because the employer has no lawful basis to retain it.

warnings: Do not omit the consent clause to match an Anglophone template. It is the one section that can void the application outright.

regions.label: Japan
regions.length: Prescribed by the form, not by you.
regions.spelling: Japanese for domestic employers; English for international firms.

notes.personal-details: The rirekisho is a standardised form with a required photo, date of birth and personal particulars. Deviating from the form is itself a negative signal.
notes.experience: The shokumu keirekisho is the separate narrative career-history document where achievements actually go.
notes.languages: JLPT level where you hold one.

warnings: A Western-style resume is not a substitute for the rirekisho at a domestic employer. Foreign-owned firms in Japan often accept a standard CV — confirm which you are applying to.

regions.label: China, Hong Kong & Singapore
regions.spelling: British English in Singapore and Hong Kong; simplified Chinese for mainland domestic employers.

notes.personal-details: Photo, date of birth and nationality are commonly included in mainland China; less so in Singapore and Hong Kong, where Anglophone norms increasingly apply.
notes.work-authorization: Singapore employment pass eligibility and Hong Kong residency status are primary screening facts. State them.
notes.languages: Mandarin and Cantonese proficiency stated precisely — spoken and written levels may differ and both matter.

warnings: Singapore's Fair Consideration Framework has moved employers away from personal particulars — when unsure there, follow the Anglophone convention.

regions.label: India
regions.docName: Resume / CV / Biodata (biodata is the older, more personal format)
regions.length: Two to three pages is accepted.

notes.personal-details: Date of birth, marital status and father's name appear in traditional formats. Modern private-sector and multinational employers do not expect them — match the employer, not the tradition.
notes.education: Percentages and class of degree are the expected grade signal. Include the board or university.
notes.additional: Notice period is conventionally stated and recruiters screen on it.

warnings: When applying to a multinational, use the international convention and drop the biodata fields.

regions.label: UAE & the Gulf

notes.personal-details: Photo, date of birth and nationality are conventional and widely expected.
notes.work-authorization: Visa status and sponsorship transferability are decisive screening facts. State current visa type and whether an NOC is required.
notes.languages: Arabic proficiency is a genuine differentiator where you have it.

warnings: Nationality materially affects hiring and packages in this market. State it, since it will be asked immediately regardless.

regions.label: Brazil & Latin America

notes.personal-details: Photo and date of birth are common. Brazil conventionally includes CPF on domestic applications.
notes.languages: English fluency is a strong differentiator — state the level precisely.
notes.education: Name the institution; regional reputation carries weight.

warnings: Never include a national identity number on an international application — only on a domestic one where it is conventional.

regions.label: South Africa

notes.referees: Commonly listed in full with contact details.
notes.personal-details: Employment-equity status is often requested on a separate form; it does not belong in the CV body.

warnings: Identity numbers are conventional domestically but should never appear on an international application.
